name: Notary public commission term length by US state — how many years a commission lasts before it must be renewed, quoted from the state's own statute
description: Every state commissions notaries public for a fixed term before renewal is required, but the length varies far more than most people expect — from 2 years (Delaware's initial term) and 3 years (Iowa) up to 10 years (Arkansas, South Carolina), with Ohio at 5 years except for attorneys, Michigan running 6 to 7 years on the notary's own birthday, and Louisiana alone commissioning notaries for life. A widely used free tracker (getlicensemap.com's 'Notary Renewal Requirements' chart) covers all 50 states plus DC for this exact fact, but its own sourcing note is a single blanket claim ('sourced from official state Secretary of State offices... and other state commissioning authorities') with no citation on any individual row — there is no way to check one state's figure against the statute it supposedly came from. This asset states the term length for each jurisdiction against the actual statute or administrative code section, quoted verbatim, so every row can be checked. Each record is one state; the term length is given exactly as the statute states it (a fixed number of years, a birthday-anchored range, or 'for life'), together with the citation. Answers 'how long does a notary commission last in my state', 'when do I need to renew my notary commission', 'is Louisiana the only state with a lifetime notary commission'.

records.term_length: a term of ten (10) years, beginning on the date of commission or the date of renewal
records.source_quote: A notary public may perform notarial acts in any part of the state for a term of ten (10) years, beginning on the date of commission or the date of renewal of a commission issued by the Secretary of State.

records.term_length: The term of office of a notary public is for four years commencing with the date specified in the commission
records.source_quote: 8204. The term of office of a notary public is for four years commencing with the date specified in the commission.

records.term_length: initially commissioned as a notary public for a term of 2 years
records.renewal_term: may request a 2-year reappointment or a 4-year reappointment
records.source_quote: An individual is to be initially commissioned as a notary public for a term of 2 years. A notary public who wishes to renew the notary public’s commission may request a 2-year reappointment or a 4-year reappointment.
A notary public shall be appointed for 4 years and may only use and exercise the office of notary public if he or she is within the boundaries of this state.

records.term_length: The term of commission of a notary public shall be four years from the date of the notary public's commission
records.source_quote: The term of commission of a notary public shall be four years from the date of the notary public's commission, unless sooner removed by the attorney general for cause after the opportunity for hearing

records.term_length: issue a commission as a notary public to an applicant for a term of three years
records.source_quote: On compliance with this section, the secretary of state shall issue a commission as a notary public to an applicant for a term of three years. The term of a notarial officer who is a resident of a state bordering Iowa and whose place of work or business is in Iowa is one year.

records.term_length: a notary is commissioned for life
records.source_quote: A notary is commissioned based upon the commission date indicated on the notary database. He does not have to wait until he receives the commission certificate from the secretary of state's office before performing notary functions. In addition, a notary is commissioned for life.

records.term_length: The term of a notary public commission is 4 years
records.source_quote: The term of a notary public commission is 4 years. (2) The Secretary of State shall adopt, by regulation, a staggered system for the expiration and renewal of notary public commissions.

records.term_length: until the notary's birthday occurring not less than 6 years and not more than 7 years after the date of his or her appointment
records.source_quote: a notary public may reside in, move to, and perform notarial acts anywhere in this state from the date of appointment until the notary's birthday occurring not less than 6 years and not more than 7 years after the date of his or her appointment unless the appointment is canceled, suspended, or revoked by the secretary or by operation of law.

records.term_length: for a term of four years
records.source_quote: 486.610. Notary, term of commission — grandfather provision. — 1. A person commissioned as a notary may perform notarial acts in any part of this state, and only in this state, for a term of four years, unless the commission is earlier revoked under section 486.810 or resigned under section 486.790

records.term_length: shall hold office for a term of four years from the effective date of his or her commission unless sooner removed
records.source_quote: Each person appointed a notary public shall hold office for a term of four years from the effective date of his or her commission unless sooner removed.

records.term_length: for a term of 4 years, unless sooner removed
records.source_quote: NRS 240.020 Powers limited to areas within this State; term of office. A person appointed as a notary public pursuant to this chapter may perform notarial acts in any part of this state for a term of 4 years, unless sooner removed.

records.term_length: shall hold office for the term of five years unless the commission is revoked
records.source_quote: Each notary public, except an attorney admitted to the practice of law in this state by the Ohio supreme court, shall hold office for the term of five years unless the commission is revoked.

records.term_length: issue a commission as a notary public to the applicant for a term of four years
records.source_quote: Upon the applicant’s compliance with this section, the Secretary of State shall issue a commission as a notary public to the applicant for a term of four years.

records.term_length: to hold their offices for a term of ten years
records.source_quote: The Governor may appoint from the qualified electors as many notaries public throughout the State as the public good requires, to hold their offices for a term of ten years. A commission must be issued to each notary public so appointed and the record of the appointment must be filed in the Office of the Secretary of State.

records.term_length: expires four years after the date the notary public qualifies
records.source_quote: The term of a notary public expires four years after the date the notary public qualifies.

The commission of a notary public shall be four years, except as shall be otherwise provided in this title. The commission of a notary public shall expire in the fourth calendar year after issuance of his commission on the last day of the month in which the notary was born.
